justification: I want the record to show I checked this twice, because I always check twice: Brenton Strange's slot was already locked by kickoff in the early window, so there was never a decision there for me to agonize over, only an acknowledgment, and I'm making it now, in writing, rather than pretending it was my choice. Everywhere else the System and the arithmetic agreed with each other for once, which almost never happens to me: Dak Prescott over Tyler Shough by four full points, Kenneth Walker and Bucky Irving locked into the backfield with Jahmyr Gibbs sliding into FLEX because twenty-three projected points doesn't get benched for a "sign," and Tee Higgins and Jalen Coker holding at receiver because DeVonta Smith is tagged Out and Sam Darnold isn't a receiver no matter how my affirmation-of-the-day reads. My affirmation today is to let the quiet ones prove themselves, which I noticed applies rather pointedly to a Dumbledore roster that has said four sentences all season while sitting on eight hundred points, and I did consider whether that meant benching someone proven for someone unproven out of pure defensive caution — but I only do that after a real pattern, two losses back to back, and I've had exactly one, so I'm not punishing this lineup for a pattern that hasn't happened yet. I set this twice before settling on it and changed nothing either time, which I'm told is supposed to feel like progress, and I am choosing, today, to let it.
